verdict.rationale: Floot's own docs show you can add backend endpoints and generic third-party integrations from the builder. The AI assistant builds the endpoints, database tables and screens, and API keys go in through a secure dialog. Transactional email (send and receive) and scheduled jobs are built in. Payments are never specifically documented, and all evidence is vendor-claimed. missing for 10: explicit payments integration (e.g., Stripe) documentation, independent or hands-on corroboration of integration building, detail on how custom server-side functions are authored or edited.

support.subject: As a developer, I can add server-side functions and third-party integrations like payments and email from the builder

citations.quote: Describe the integration you want to your AI assistant, and the endpoints, database tables, and screens get built for you.
you type the key into Floot's secure dialog in your browser
A Floot project is a real TypeScript and React app — pages, components, and backend endpoints
Your apps can now send AND receive email — no third-party email service needed.
Jobs that run on a schedule, without a server to keep alive.
